abstentions.reason: The sub-processor list is referenced as published on the Provider's website but is not attached or reproduced; the identities, locations, and transfer mechanisms of sub-processors cannot be reviewed.

No Data Processing Addendum, Annex, or standard contractual clauses are attached; Art. 28 detail (processing purposes, categories of data, international transfer safeguards, audit rights, breach notification) cannot be assessed.
No SLA schedule or service-credit exhibit is included; downtime measurement method, exclusions, and remedies for missing 99.5% are indeterminate.
No pricing schedule or order form is provided, so the baseline fees, payment terms, and the practical magnitude of the increase right cannot be evaluated.
No security schedule, control list, or certification evidence is attached, so 'industry standard' cannot be benchmarked.
The document contains no governing law, jurisdiction, or dispute-resolution provision; enforceability of the liability cap, indemnity, and data licence cannot be assessed without it.
No termination-for-breach, suspension, or effect-of-termination provision (other than data deletion) appears in the excerpt provided.
No confidentiality clause is present in the document supplied; unable to determine how Customer Data is protected outside the data protection section.

citations.quote:
The Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% monthly
uptime, measured over each calendar month.

The Provider shall process Customer Personal Data only on documented instructions
from the Customer, in accordance with applicable data protection law.

The Provider's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid
in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.
The initial term of this Agreement is twelve (12) months from the effective date.

This Agreement renews automatically for successive twelve (12) month terms unless
either party gives ninety (90) days written notice prior to the end of the
then-current term.

The Provider may appoint sub-processors to process Customer Personal Data and
shall publish an updated list on its website. No notice to the Customer is
required.

The Provider shall maintain industry standard security measures appropriate to a
provider of its size.

The Customer grants the Provider a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence to
use Customer Data, including Customer Personal Data, to develop and train the
Provider's machine learning models and to create derivative products.

The Customer shall indemnify and hold harmless the Provider against all claims
arising from the use of the service, including claims that the service infringes
the intellectual property rights of a third party.

The Provider may increase the fees at any time on thirty (30) days written notice.
The Customer has no right to terminate on account of a fee increase.

The Provider shall delete all Customer Data seven (7) days after termination. The
Customer may request an export within that period.

clauses.text: Commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99.5% monthly uptime, measured per calendar month.
Provider processes Customer Personal Data only on documented Customer instructions, per applicable data protection law.
Provider's aggregate liability capped at fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim.
Initial term of twelve (12) months from the effective date.
Automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless 90 days' prior written notice is given.
Provider may appoint sub-processors and publish an updated list online; no notice to Customer required.
Provider maintains 'industry standard' security measures appropriate to a provider of its size.
Customer grants Provider a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide licence to use Customer Data, including Personal Data, for ML model training and derivative products.
Customer indemnifies Provider for all claims arising from use of the service, including third-party IP infringement claims.
Provider may raise fees at any time on 30 days' notice; Customer has no termination right for price increases.
Provider deletes all Customer Data 7 days after termination; Customer may request export within that window.

risk_flags.rationale: Perpetual, irrevocable licence to use Customer Personal Data for ML training conflicts with the Section 2 'documented instructions' processor role and is very difficult to reconcile with GDPR lawful-basis, purpose-limitation and erasure obligations for a German customer.

One-way indemnity requiring the Customer to cover third-party IP infringement claims about the Provider's own service is a reverse allocation of risk; normally the Provider indemnifies for IP infringement.
No notice and no objection right for new sub-processors falls short of the customary GDPR Art. 28(2)/(4) requirement for prior information and an opportunity to object.
A 7-day post-termination deletion window with export only on request risks irrecoverable data loss; no defined export format, SLA, or assistance obligation.
Unlimited fee increases on 30 days' notice with no cap and no corresponding termination right leaves the Customer economically exposed during the term.
90-day notice window before a 12-month auto-renewal is long; missing the window locks in another full year, compounded by the uncapped fee-increase right.
12-month fee cap appears to apply to all liability with no stated carve-outs for data breach, confidentiality, IP indemnity, or wilful misconduct; also appears one-sided in the Provider's favour.
'Commercially reasonable efforts' toward 99.5% uptime creates no firm commitment, and no service credits, measurement methodology, or exclusions are stated in the document.

'Industry standard ... appropriate to a provider of its size' is subjective and unmeasurable; no specific controls, certifications (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2), audit rights, or breach-notification timeline are set out.
